Were Analysts Bullish Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:ZBH) This Week?
November 5, 2018 - By Richard Slagle Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:ZBH) Ratings Coverage
Among 13 analysts covering Zimmer Biomet Holdings ( NYSE:ZBH ), 6 have Buy rating, 2 Sell and 5 Hold. Therefore 46% are positive. Zimmer Biomet Holdings had 15 analyst reports since June 22, 2018 according to SRatingsIntel. Barclays Capital maintained Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:ZBH) rating on Monday, October 29. Barclays Capital has “Underweight” rating and $119 target. The firm has “Market Outperform” rating given on Monday, July 30 by JMP Securities. The firm has “Overweight” rating given on Thursday, October 11 by Morgan Stanley. As per Monday, July 30, the company rating was maintained by Raymond James. The stock of Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:ZBH) has “Neutral” rating given on Monday, July 30 by Robert W. Baird. As per Tuesday, July 31, the company rating was maintained by Citigroup. As per Friday, June 22, the company rating was downgraded by Argus Research. As per Monday, July 30, the company rating was maintained by Cantor Fitzgerald. Needham downgraded Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:ZBH) on Monday, August 13 to “Buy” rating. The firm has “Neutral” rating by Citigroup given on Monday, October 29. The stock decreased 1.35% or $1.58 during the last trading session, reaching $115.14. About 1.10M shares traded or 4.88% up from the average. Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:ZBH) has risen 8.38% since November 5, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 7.24% the S&P500.
Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, designs, makes, and markets musculoskeletal healthcare products and solutions in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. The company has market cap of $23.49 billion. It operates through four divisions: Americas Spine, Office Based Technologies, Craniomaxillofacial and Thoracic , and Dental. It has a 13.93 P/E ratio. The firm provides orthopedic reconstructive products, such as knee and hip reconstructive products; S.E.T. products, including surgical, sports medicine, biologics, foot and ankle, extremities, and trauma products; spine products comprising medical devices and surgical instruments; and face and skull reconstruction products, as well as products that fixate and stabilize the bones of the chest to facilitate healing or reconstruction after open heart surgery, trauma, or for deformities of the chest.
